_comment: Expectations for the automated worldgen check. Add a body by adding an entry
under 'bodies' — the harness in scripts/worldgen-check.py needs no change.
See docs/testing/worldgen-registry-check.md.
Electro's `ore_veins` is an empty object on purpose, and the emptiness is the
assertion: no vein in the loaded registry may reach this dimension. The body is
barren by design — its economy is recycling. See docs/adr/0009-electro-registers-no-ore-veins.md.
Fulgorite and scrap piles are placed features, not veins, and so are not checked here.
Not a body: a vanilla dimension the pack strips of GregTech worldgen (ADR-0007, #16).
The three empty objects are assertions — the check walks the whole registry for each, so
a vein or deposit that later reaches this dimension fails here rather than silently
restoring the stock progression. Vanilla generation is untouched and is not checked.
Not a body: a vanilla dimension the pack strips of GregTech worldgen (ADR-0007, #16).
The three empty objects are assertions — the check walks the whole registry for each, so
a vein or deposit that later reaches this dimension fails here rather than silently
restoring the stock progression. Vanilla generation is untouched and is not checked.
Sapros is barren of veins and of both kinds of bedrock deposit, and all three empty
objects are assertions rather than omissions — the check walks the whole registry for
each. It differs from Electro's emptiness: Electro has no metal at all, where Sapros has
metal that arrives by Decaying a bacterium taken from a stromatolite (ADR-0016). Until the
Decay engine (#17) ships, that metal is unobtainable, and that is the design.
Stromatolites are placed features, not veins, so they are not checked here.
The five biomes are: a biome that parses but occupies unreachable noise space generates
nowhere, and only the generator can tell the two apart.
Terra after #58: four ore veins, iron then copper then coal with uranium rare, all on
the `stone` layer inside ADR-0019's shallow band. The `deepslate` layer is gone, and so
is every other vein -- `forbidden_ore_veins` names each one, because a cut here is an
absent file (kubejs/data/remove-terra-cut-veins.zip filters GregTech's own) and a file
that comes back reverts the decision without touching anything this fixture would
otherwise read. ADR-0019's other two claims -- the terrain is flat, no caves generate --
are invisible to every registry and are checked by a human on delivery.
Terra's bedrock carries oil and nothing else (#86). The only depleting-but-never-gone
resource in Factorio is oil, so the bedrock set is one authored crude deposit and no ore
at all -- the coal and uranium deposits ADR-0021 named are not built, and the iron and
copper ones that did exist are deleted, an infinite ore patch being no more a Factorio
object at a yield of 4 than at 40. Both ADR-0021 and ADR-0020's tail are amended.
`bedrock_ores` is an empty object on purpose and the emptiness is the assertion: the
check walks the whole registry, so a deposit that later reaches the overworld without
naming itself here fails. The fractions are the Oil Refinery's job (ADR-0025), so the six stock GregTech
fluid deposits that shipped to the overworld are narrowed to nowhere by an override
carrying an empty `dimension_filter`, and each is named in `forbidden_bedrock_fluids`
-- an override that goes missing restores GregTech's whole spread in silence.
No `set` and no `placement`: this structure is not placed by worldgen at all. Vanilla has
no spawn-anchored placement type and cannot have one -- a StructurePlacement decides from
ChunkGeneratorStructureState alone, which carries no world spawn -- so planetaryfactory_core
stamps the pool onto spawn on ServerStartedEvent. What is still worth asserting here is what
the stamp depends on: that the structure loaded, that its biomes are ones Terra emits, and
that the three ore ids it is built from are real registered blocks rather than plausible
near misses that would silently place air.
